transitions.device_described: Dell PowerEdge R720 (Grid'5000 Lyon 'Taurus' node; 2x Intel Xeon E5-2630, 32 GB)
transitions.derivation: Modeled 'suspend/wake' = ACPI S5 shutdown/boot exactly as measured (the cited lineage reports S3 suspend-to-RAM unsupported on these servers: Rais et al., CCPE 2018, DOI 10.1002/cpe.4471). suspend := On->Off (T=15 s, E=1655 J), wake := Off->On (T=182 s, E=23683 J), suspended draw := Poff = 8 W. Published transition-energy totals are used directly as the simulator's transition pulses; the simulator additionally meters idle-level draw during the transition window, so the modeled transition cost upper-bounds the published measurement by at most Pidle*T (conservative against suspension churn).

provenance.source_name: Benoit, Lefevre, Orgerie & Rais, 'Reducing the energy consumption of large scale computing systems through combined shutdown policies with multiple constraints', IJHPCA 32(1):176-188, 2018
provenance.field_transcribed: Table 3 ('Calibration node characteristics and energy parameters for On->Off and Off->On sequences (average on 50 experimental measurements)'): EOffOn 23683 J, TOffOn 182 s, EOnOff 1655 J, TOnOff 15 s, Pidle 91 W, Poff 8 W.
provenance.verification_method: author-hosted PDF fetched 2026-07-16; the values 23683, 1655, 182, 286.29 independently re-extracted from the PDF text in a second pass; HAL bibliographic record confirmed via api.archives-ouvertes.fr (hal-01557025)
provenance.notes: Transition measurements are class-level published data from a different machine than the SPECpower power-curve machines (no source publishes both); bundles state this composition explicitly (plan section 4.1: tuple = power curve + capacity; transition table attaches per bundle).

transitions.device_described: Dell PowerEdge R630 (Grid'5000 'Paravance' node; Intel Xeon E5-2630v3)
transitions.derivation: Modeled 'suspend/wake' = ACPI S5 regular shutdown/boot exactly as measured ('values for regular shutdown, S5 mode (average of 100 run)'). suspend := On->Off (T=7.5 s, E=2000 J), wake := Off->On (T=167.5 s, E=19893 J), suspended draw := Poff = 4.5 W. Same pulse semantics as transition-taurus-ijhpca2018.

provenance.source_name: Rais, Orgerie & Quinson, 'Impact of Shutdown Techniques for Energy-Efficient Cloud Data Centers', ICA3PP 2016 (Springer), pp. 203-210
provenance.field_transcribed: Table 1 ('average on 100 experimental measurements'), Paravance column: EOffOn 19,893 J, EOnOff 2,000 J, TOffOn 167.5 s, TOnOff 7.5 s, Pidle 150 W, Poff 4.5 W; hardware row: Dell PowerEdge R630, Xeon E5-2630v3.

boavizta_scope_deviation: R1-4/R2-7 documented scope deviation, no coefficient entry pinned: Boavizta (BoaviztAPI v2.3.0, queried 2026-07-18) publishes an instance-specific consumption-profile impact model (nonlinear host power from CPU profiles, allocated by vCPU and memory ratios) — not a scalar per-vCPU-hour coefficient, and not the linear min/max-utilization interpolation this schema's cloud_allocation entries model (CCF's usage). Pinning a scalar here would model Boavizta through a functional form it does not publish. The raw API response for AWS m5.xlarge is retained at artifacts/boaviztapi-aws-m5xlarge-2026-07-18.json (sha256 5c09fab320a3226d18c9db6bfb567307e126fc54056144d2fdb95d076275907b) as evidence for the P2 bundle-list decision on whether a Boavizta consumption-profile bundle family (a separate structural family with its own model code) is added.
